purpose:
Report to inform cabinet of the final outturn
position for the Council against the budget for 2025-26.
content:
RESOLVED
that:-
 

Cabinet approve:
1.1         
The net re-profiling to the Capital Programme of £60.971
million from 2025-26 to 2026-27 to reflect expenditure levels
during the financial year.
1.2         
The use of reserves shown at
Appendix K.
Cabinet
note:

1.3         
The final outturn is based upon the
draft Statement of Accounts and is subject to external
audit.

The net change on the General Fund compared to the Provisional
Outturn of £0.183 million which was transferred

service and the overall council position.

The
projected overspend on the Dedicated Schools Grant of £12.061
million as detailed in Appendix D.
1.7         
The
projected overspend on the Housing Revenue Account (HRA) budget of
£0.102 million as detailed in Appendix I.
1.8         
The delivery of the approved
savings at Appendix A. 
1.9         
The details of capital project
reprofiling shown at Appendix L.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to re-profile the Capital Programme budget and use reserves to reflect expenditure levels during the financial year.

purpose:

from stakeholders arising from statutory consultation regardng the
formalisation of specialst support bases.
content:

that in light of the prescribed changes set out in
the statutory proposals published on 9 April 2026 (attached at
Appendix 1a-c) and the information provided in the report, and in
accordance with the Statutory Guidance from the Department for
Education “Making significant changes (‘prescribed

purpose:
Approval is sought to revise the previously
approved scheme cost and funding package for the A193 Seafront
Active Travel Scheme, and to amend the capital programme
accordingly. Authority is also sought to finalise external funding
arrangements and enter into the necessary contracts to enable
delivery, subject to confirmation of funding.
content:
RESOLVED
that Cabinet:-
 
a)   
approve the revised scheme cost of £13.488
million for the A193 Seafront Active Travel Scheme, replacing the
previously approved allocation of £9.688 million;
 
b)   
approve the revised funding package,
comprising:
·      
£11.740 million North East Mayoral Strategic
Authority grant funding from CRSTS; and
·      
£1.748 million Council resources;
 
c)    
approve the amendment to the Medium Term Financial
Plan to reflect the revised scheme cost and funding profile as set
out in Table 1, in section 5 of this report;
 
d)   
delegate authority to the Executive Director for
Place and Regeneration, in consultation with the Executive Director
for Transformation and Resources (S151 Officer), to:
·      
finalise funding arrangements with the North East
Mayoral Strategic Authority; and
·      
enter into all necessary contracts within the
approved budget allocation;
 
e)   
note that delivery remains subject to confirmation
of external funding and that the Council contribution is profiled
towards the latter stages of the scheme; and
 
f)     
note that the Council contribution of £1.748
million is not new budget provision and comprises:
·      
£1.453 million previously approved by Cabinet
on 8 July 2025 and County Council on 18 February 2026;
and
·    
£0.295 million from existing Local Transport
Plan commitments.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve a revised scheme cost and funding package for the A193 Seafront Active Travel Scheme.

purpose:
The report seeks cabinet approval to the key
terms for the selection of a developer to acquire, and deliver key
outcomes on this council owned site.
content:
RESOLVED that Cabinet agree the
following:-
 
3.1.1   
   the
procurement process be progressed with a view to the disposal of
the former Hexham Middle School site (the “Site”) to
the preferred bidder to develop the Site in accordance with the
detail set out herein, which will achieve best consideration in
accordance with the assessment criteria;
 
3.1.2
    authority be delegated to
the Executive Director– Place and Regeneration, in
consultation with the Deputy Leader and the Director of Law &
Corporate Governance to
 
3.1.2.1
   appoint a developer to develop
the site following the procurement exercise undertaken in
accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 and the Council’s
own Finance and Contract Rules, 
 
3.1.2.2

agreements [CB1] and contracts as may be required to
secure the delivery of the objectives as set out in this report for

compliance with eligibility criteria in accordance with the
AA&W Fund and identified viability gap;
 
3.1.5

authority to the Executive Director of Adults Services and Health

Executive Director of Transformation and Resources to approve the

viability assessment; and

of the site by way of Freehold Title transfer to the preferred
bidder following contract award as set out in paragraph 3.1.1

purpose:

that:-
 
(a)      Cabinet accepts, on a
comparative assessment of public interest needs, that the NCC Open
Space Land (as identified in the plan and schedule in Appendices A
and B of the Land Appropriation Background Report) is no longer
required for the purpose of open space for which it is currently
held;
 
(b)      Cabinet authorises the
publication of notices required by section 122(2A) LGA 1972 and
records that it is minded for the Council to appropriate the NCC
Open Space Land for planning purposes (within section 246(1) of the
TCPA 1990) to facilitate the construction and operation of the
Chase Farm Link, engaging the statutory override mechanism under
section 203 HPA 2016, subject to and following the section 122
process and consideration of any representations received;
and

the Executive Director – Place and Regeneration
to:

undertake the statutory advertising process required by section
122(2A) LGA 1972;
 
•         consider
any objections or representations received in response to the
statutory advertisements and decide, following such consideration,
whether to proceed with the appropriation of the NCC Open Space
Land (or any part thereof) for highway use; and
 
•         take all
necessary steps to implement the recommendations set out in this
Report, including the settlement of any compensation claims under
section 204 HPA 2016, and any other action required to give effect
to the appropriation and enable the delivery of the
Scheme.

purpose:
Report to inform cabinet of the provisional
outturn for the Council against budget for 2025-26.
content:
RESOLVED
that:-
 
Cabinet approve:
 
3.1     The creation of a new earmarked
reserve for the Northumberland Children and Adults Safeguarding
Partnership (NCASP) which is hosted by the Council. The Partnership
is jointly funded by Northumberland County Council, Northumbria
Police and North East & North Cumbria Integrated Care Board. It
has been agreed by all parties that the unspent balance of funds at
the end of 2025-26 will be carried forward to support ongoing
safeguarding work in 2026-27. This reserve will hold the balance of
the Council contribution remaining at the end of 2025-26 which is
expected to be £0.039 million. This arrangement will be
reviewed on an annual basis.
 
3.2     The creation of a new earmarked
reserve within the Housing Revenue Account for demolition costs of
unused dwellings. The reserve will hold the balance from the
£0.600 million that was set aside within the 2025-26 budget,
with expenditure being planned for early 2026-27.
 
3.3     The drawdown of £1.509
million from the Strategic Management earmarked reserve and
£0.686 million from the Restructuring Reserve to meet the
voluntary redundancy, severance and strain on the fund costs
associated with those staff leaving the Council as part of the Ways
of Working restructure. This covers the costs incurred during
2025-26 and the provision made for those staff due to leave in
2026-27 that meet the redundancy provision criteria.
 
3.4     The drawdown of £0.996
million from the Homes for Ukraine Scheme earmarked reserve, which
has been used to support Ukrainian families to rebuild their lives
and fully integrate into local communities.
 
3.5     The transfer of £2.000
million to the Dedicated Schools Grant (DSG) Deficit reserve. The
Council is required to meet 10% of the cumulative DSG deficit at 31
March 2028, when the statutory override is due to end. This
contribution represents 10% of the cumulative deficit at 31 March
2026, with the remaining 90% to be met by the High Needs Stability
Grant which is expected in 2026-27.
 
3.6     The amendment to the funding
package for the Northumberland Line and Newsham Railway Bridge
by:
 
i.        Reallocating
£0.500 million of Council funding from the Northumberland
Line project to the Newsham Road Bridge project.
ii.        Reallocating
£0.500 million from the sum allocated in the Strategic
Management Reserve for the Newsham Road Bridge project to fund the
benefits realisation studies within the Council’s revenue
budget.
 
3.7     That approval be delegated to
the Section 151 Officer to authorise the utilisation of any balance
remaining, upon finalisation of the Statement of Accounts, to be
transferred to/from council reserves.
 
3.8     The transfer of £0.818
million to the Restructuring Reserve to meet future costs linked to
the Voluntary Exit Scheme in 2026-27.
 
Cabinet note:
 
3.9     The projected breakeven position
on services and the assumptions outlined in this report.
 
3.10    That the provisional outturn position
may change and it is subject to the impact of any technical
accounting adjustments required in finalising the statement of
accounts.
 
3.11    The projected overspend on the
Dedicated Schools Grant of £11.991 million as detailed in
Appendix E.
 
3.12    The projected overspend on the Housing
Revenue Account (HRA) budget of £0.102 million as detailed in
Appendix J.
 
3.13    The re-profiling to the Capital
Programme of £60.940 million from 2025-26 to 2026-27 to
reflect the outturn in the current financial year.
 
3.14    The supplementary estimates at
Appendix A and the required changes to the budgets.
 
3.15    The delivery of the approved savings
at Appendix B.
 
3.16    The use of the contingency shown at
Appendix L.
 
3.17    The use of reserves shown at Appendix
M.
 
3.18    The virements requested by services
within delegated limits as shown in Appendix N.
 
3.19    The details of capital project
reprofiling shown at Appendix O.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to create new earmarked reserves and transfer funds to address various financial needs in Northumberland.

purpose:
??This report provides Cabinet with an update
on the Borderlands Inclusive Growth Deal, including delivery to
date, future proposed delivery, and changes to the accountable body
arrangements that Northumberland County Council perform on behalf
of the English councils.
content:
RESOLVED:
 
 

Cabinet note the
progress being made on delivery of the Borderlands Inclusive Growth
Deal through Northumberland’s three major programmes to date;
Northumberland Borderlands Place Programme, Northumberland
Borderlands Inclusive Growth Programme and Borderlands Energy
Programme

 

Cabinet support the
ongoing development and mobilisation of investment propositions as
set out in the report, and agree the following:

Approve the
appropriation for planning purposes of the Council's Land at The
Maltings Theatre, Berwick-upon-Tweed pursuant to Section 122 Local
Government Act 1972 and the subsequent engagement and use of the
powers under Section 203 Housing and Planning Act 2016, as set out
in para 7.36.
Submission of the
Northumberland Hadrian’s Wall Visitor Exploration Project
Full Business Case to Borderlands for appraisal and, subject to the
outcome of the appraisal, delegate authority to the Executive
Director of Transformation and Resources (s151 Officer) to accept
funding from the Borderlands Partnership for delivery.
Confirm approval of
the Borderlands’ Energy Programme Business Case and
shortlisting process and Borderlands’ Hadrian’s Wall
Programme Business Case which have been approved by the Borderlands
Partnership Board.
Delegate authority to
the Executive Director of Place and Regeneration, in consultation
with the Portfolio Holder for Business, Growth and Regeneration, to
undertake all necessary procurement activity associated with the
Northumberland Hadrian’s Wall Visitor Exploration Programme,
subject to approval of the full business case.
Agree that a
subsequent report relating to the Northumberland Borderlands Energy
Programme will be brought back to Cabinet, with authority delegated
as above to undertake preparatory and development
activity.



 

As part of
implementing the Borderlands ‘Reset’, Cabinet delegate
authority to the Executive Director of Transformation and Resources
(s151 Officer) in conjunction with the Cabinet Member for Business,
Growth and Regeneration to approve project drawdowns, programme
reallocations, change controls and statutory financial returns, in
alignment with Northumberland County Council’s Local
Assurance Framework.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve various actions related to the Borderlands Inclusive Growth Deal in Northumberland.

purpose:
This report seeks approval
to commence a procurement exercise for the development of
extra care schemes on Council owned sites in
Northumberland
content:
RESOLVED that:-
 
(a)      Cabinet grant permission to
undertake the necessary procurements to enable Northumberland
County Council to contract with Registered Social Landlords to
deliver extra care schemes at 4 Council owned sites including
Alnwick, Ashington, Cramlington and Blyth;
(b)     Cabinet delegate authority to
the Council’s Executive Director – Adults Ageing and
Wellbeing to approve the award of contracts following this
procurement process, with the agreement of the Executive Director
of Transformation & Resources and the Cabinet Member for Adult
Care & Health;
(c)      Cabinet approve the inclusion of
the Council owned sites listed at para 4.4 as part of the
procurement process, and the subsequent delegated disposal of sites
in accordance with the outcome of the procurement process; and
(d)     Cabinet delegate authority to
the Executive Director of Place and Regeneration in consultation
with the Cabinet Member for Business, Growth & Regeneration for
individual site disposals, provided those decisions are consistent
with the legal advice received and referenced in this report, on
the disposal of Council owned assets. Where land receipt for any
site is greater than £1 million this will require Cabinet
approval.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to grant permission for extra care schemes at 4 Council owned sites in Northumberland.

that:-

and

purpose:
Cabinet is asked to authorise the making of a
Compulsory Purchase Order (“CPO”) and Side Road Order
(“SRO”) for the purpose of delivering the Blyth Relief
Road Scheme.
content:
RESOLVED
that:-
 
(a)     Cabinet authorise the making of
a Compulsory Purchase Order (CPO) for the purpose of the Scheme and
pursuant to sections 239, 240, 246 and 250 of the
Highways Act 1980 (‘Highways Act’) and all
other powers as appropriate to acquire the land and rights shown on
the draft Order Maps (Appendix A.2) and to implement
the CPO;
(b)     Cabinet authorise the making of
a Side Roads Order (SRO) under sections 14 and 125 of the Highways
Act and all other necessary powers to improve, and stop up existing
highway, construct a new highway and stop up and provide a
new private means of access (PMA) as shown on the
draft SRO maps and all other powers as
appropriate to implement the
SRO (Appendix B.2);
(c)      authority be delegated to
the Executive Director of Place and Regeneration to take all
necessary steps, and to enter into all documentation, on behalf of
the Council in connection with the making, confirmation, submission
or implementation of the Orders, including in respect of service of
all relevant notices, any public inquiry, appeal or legal challenge
concerning the Scheme;
(d)     authority be delegated to the
Executive Director of Place and Regeneration to remove from the
Orders any plot or interest therein no longer to be acquired
compulsorily and make amendments to the Orders and other connected
documents provided that the proposed amendments do not
significantly alter the scope of the Orders as presented to the
Committee by this Report; and
(e )     Cabinet note the making of
applications under section 248 and section 257 of the Town and
Country Planning Act in order to stop up or stop up and divert
highways as necessary that cross or enter the route of the Chase
Farm Link, and stop up and divert a footpath, noting that such
applications can only be made once planning permission for the
Chase Farm Link has been granted.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to authorize the making of a Compulsory Purchase Order and Side Roads Order for a highway scheme.

that:-

Cabinet note the purpose of Local Plan Scoping

purpose:
To receive the Institute of Health Equity's
Report on Reducing Inequalities in Northumberland through
Employment
content:
RESOLVED
that:-
(a)      Cabinet endorse the Institute of
Health Equity’s Report on Reducing Inequalities in Health in
Northumberland through Employment;
(b)      Cabinet note the findings from
the report which provides an independent assessment to Cabinet with
a clear, evidence-based set of recommendations to inform decisions
on actions that are most likely to reduce the healthy life
expectancy gap in Northumberland by improving equity of access to
good quality employment; and

Northumberland County Council alongside a wider set of partners and
the mechanisms which will be used to deliver the recommendations in
the report.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to endorse a report on reducing inequalities in health in Northumberland through employment

purpose:
This report summarises proposed amendments to
the capital programme considered by the Capital Strategy Group on
24 February 2026.
content:
RESOLVED
that Cabinet agree as follows:-
 

Kitchen Supply Framework

·     
Approve the expenditure of £2.500 million,
spread over 4 years, for the replacement of kitchens within 1,600
Council-owned homes. This expenditure will be funded from the Major
Repairs Reserve in the Housing Revenue Account.

·     
Grant delegated authority to the Executive Director
of Place and Regeneration to enter into the resulting single
supplier framework contract for the project up to a value of
£2.500 million.

East Hartford Internal Refurbishment

·     
Approve the expenditure of £9.309 million,
spread over 4 years, for the internal refurbishment of 95
Council-owned homes. This expenditure will be funded from the Major
Repairs Reserve in the Housing Revenue Account.

·     
Grant delegated authority to the Executive
Director of Place and Regeneration to enter
into a resulting contract for the project, up
to the value of £6.489 million.

Blyth Civic Centre

·     
Approve the expenditure of £5.788 million in
2026-27 for the redevelopment of Blyth Civic Centre to provide an
80-place education setting (40 Alternative Provision and 40 Post-16
Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND) places), with
opportunities for evening and weekend community use. This
expenditure will be funded £2.400 million from the Department
for Education (DfE) grant, £0.488 million from Section 106
funding and £2.900 million from the existing Special
Educational Needs Capacity Growth capital project. The £2.900
million is made up of existing DfE funding of £2.400 million
and £0.500 million of Council funding.

·     
Approve the amendment to the capital programme to
add in the DfE funding of £2.400 million and the Section 106
funding of £0.488 million in 2026-27.

·     
Approve the amendment to the capital programme to
reallocate £2.900 million (£2.400 million DfE grant and
£0.500 million Council funding) from the Special Educational
Needs Capacity Growth capital project to the Blyth Civic Centre
project in 2026-27.

Northumberland Playzone
Programme – Portfolio 2

·     
Approve the expenditure of £0.629 million
(£0.005 million in 2025-26 and £0.624 million in
2026-27) for the development of two Playzones. This expenditure will be funded
£0.437 million from the Football Foundation grant,
£0.123 million from Council funding from the existing
Northumberland Playzones project in the
capital programme and £0.069 million Section 106
funding.

·     
Approve the amendment to the capital programme to
add in the Football Foundation grant funding of £0.437
million in 2026-27 and the Section 106 funding of £0.005
million in 2025-26 and £0.064 million in 2026-27.

Monitor Replacement Programme

·     
Approve the expenditure of £0.300 million
(£0.200 million in 2026-27 and £0.100 million in
2027-28) for the replacement of computer monitors across Council
buildings. This expenditure will be Council funded from the
existing Device Replacement project included in the capital
programme.

Woodhorn Phase 1

·     
Approve the expenditure of £0.400 million for
the detailed technical design for the Woodhorn Powering the Past
and the Future project. This expenditure will be Council funded
from the existing Energy Efficiency project in the capital
programme.

Bus Service Improvement Plans

·     
Approve the expenditure of £1.814 million in
2026-27 for the construction of the Bus Service Improvement Plan
Alnwick Bus Station Safety and Accessibility Improvements Scheme.
This expenditure will be funded from a grant from the North East
Combined Authority.

·     
Approve the amendment to the capital programme to
add in the £1.814 million external funding in 2026-27 for the
Bus Service Improvement Plan Alnwick Bus Station Safety and
Accessibility Improvements Scheme.

·     
Grant delegated authority to the Executive Director
for Place and Regeneration to enter into the grant funding
agreement.

Residential Homes for Children Programme –
Short Breaks

·     
Approve the expenditure of £1.900 million in
2026-27 for the development of an in-house short breaks provision.
This expenditure will be funded from the existing Residential Homes
for Children project in the capital programme.

·      
Grant delegated authority to the Executive Director
for Children, Young People and Education to enter into a contract
for the works and services up to a value of £1.900
million.

purpose:
In accordance with the Energising Blyth
Programme - Local Assurance Framework, the report seeks the
approval of the Full Business Case (FBC) for the Energy Central
Campus Phase 2: Energy Central Institute.
content:
RESOLVED that:-
 

Where NCC is a member of Energy Central Campus
Limited (ECC Ltd) and is acting as guarantor to the NECA/ECC Ltd
Grant Funding Agreement, Cabinet agrees to :

3.1.1  Amend the
delegation granted by Cabinet on 11th February 2025 (as
set out in the report dated 11.02.2025) to read:

Vary the existing Members & Framework Agreement
to reflect NCC’s role as contracting authority for the
capital build, to confirm reimbursement arrangements up to the
value of the NECA capital grant, and to incorporate VAT
related provisions including NCC’s option to tax, the
VAT treatment of NCC funded works, VAT
inclusive invoicing, and ECC Ltd’s need for
sufficient cashflow to meet VAT obligations prior to
reimbursement; and to set out clear responsibilities for the
delivery of outputs and outcomes required by all GFAs.

3.1.2  Delegate authority
to the Executive Director for Place & Regeneration, in
consultation with the Executive Director of Transformation and
Resources, subject to subsidy control compliance, to enter into an
unsecured Facility Agreement or such amendments to the Members
& Framework Agreement as may be appropriate to provide
funds to ECC Ltd up to a maximum sum of £200,000 (an increase
from £100,000 in the current Members & Framework
Agreement) to be funded from the Regeneration Reserve Development
Fund (RRDF), subject to equal
value facility agreement being made
by the other two founding partners of ECC
Ltd.

Where NCC is the applicant and Grant Funding
Recipient for FHSF and Town Deal capital
funding Cabinet agrees to:

3.2.1    
Delegate authority to the Executive Director for
Place & Regeneration, in consultation with the Executive
Director of Transformation and Resources and the Deputy Leader as
Portfolio Holder to enter into a Grant Funding Agreement between
Northumberland County Council as the Grant Funding Recipient and
Northumberland County Council as NCC Accountable Body.

3.2.2    
Delegate authority to the Executive Director for
Place & Regeneration in consultation with the Executive
Director of Transformation and Resources and the Portfolio Holder,
to enter into any contracts relating to the project subject to
confirmation of associated funding being in place and the
appropriate procurement processes being followed.

3.2.3  Delegate authority
to the Executive Director for Place & Regeneration in
consultation with the Executive Director of Transformation and
Resources and the Portfolio Holder, to place early orders from
April 2026 as detailed in the report up to the value of
£2,182,400 under the existing Pre-Construction Services
Agreement, but prior to entering into the main build contract with,
Kier Construction Ltd (see paras 5.30-5.45 below) subject to
appropriate procurement processes being followed.

In relation to NCC as the Accountable Body for the
Town Deal funding Cabinet agrees to:
3.3.1 
Delegate authority, in accordance with the Local
Assurance Framework, to the Executive
Director of Transformation and Resources following consideration of the recommendation of the NCC
Programme Board to approve the Full Business Case.
This includes the updated total project cost of
£24.869m as set out in table 3a with
the funding available to meet those costs as identified in table
3b.
 
3.3.2  Delegate authority to the
Executive Director of Transformation and Resources to enter into a
Grant Funding Agreement between Northumberland County Council as
the fund Accountable Body and Northumberland County Council as the
applicant/funding recipient, subject
to satisfactory appraisal and Subsidy Control
compliance.

In relation to NCC’s role as landowner and
freeholder of Energy Central Institute, Cabinet agrees
to: 

3.4.1  Delegate authority
to the Executive Director for Place & Regeneration to enter
into, an agreement for lease and long lease arrangement with ECC
Ltd for the land/building at nil consideration subject to
compliance with the Local Government Act 1972, permitted use
requirements and Subsidy Control advice. The terms of such lease
ensure that NCC as recipient of grant funding is able to comply
with the GFA conditions.

3.4.2  Approve updates to
the capital programme as set out in table 3b including the
reallocation of £3,879,164 NCC match fund currently allocated
in the MTFP for a proposed hotel to ECI and an allocation of
£1,000,000 from the Northumberland Growth Fund (NGF) in
2026/27 to the ECI.

purpose:
Report to set out revised Northumberland
Economic Strategy and Investment Framework for the Growth and
Investment Endowment Fund.
content:
RESOLVED
that:-
 
(a)      Cabinet endorse the
Northumberland Economic Strategy 2035 recognising the Strategy as
the overarching framework for driving economic growth in
Northumberland over the next decade;
 
(b)      Cabinet note the findings
from the independent assessment undertaken to provide Cabinet with
a clear, evidence-based framework to inform decisions on how the
Northumberland Growth Fund resources should be deployed over
time;
 
(c)      Cabinet note that a
separate report will be presented to Cabinet on Reducing
Inequalities in Health in Northumberland through Work, a report
commissioned from the Institute of Health Equity;
 
(d)      Cabinet approve the
approach set out in this report for the Northumberland Growth Fund,
including the proposed investment programmes and funds, governance
arrangements, prioritisation framework and monitoring and
evaluation approach, as the basis for mobilising investment in
support of the Economic Strategy;
 
(e )     Cabinet approve the following
capital funding allocation from the Northumberland Growth
Fund:
a)      
£8.25m to establish a Northumberland Economic Infrastructure
Programme as a phased early investment programme to be administered
by Northumberland County Council in order
to maintain momentum and secure early economic
benefits.
b)      
£20m to establish a Business Northumberland Investment Fund
as an externally managed recyclable fund. £10m to be
allocated from the funds already received and £10m from
future instalments;
 
(f)       authority be
delegated to the Executive Director of Place and Regeneration, in
consultation with the Northumberland County Council Programme
Board, the Deputy Leader and the Leader to administer the
Northumberland Economic Infrastructure Programme and make relevant
funding decisions in relation to the £8.25m initial
programme;
 
(g)      authority be delegated to
the Executive Director of Place and Regeneration, in consultation
with the Executive Director of Transformation and Resources, to
progress the necessary steps to establish the Northumberland
Business Growth Fund;
 
(h)      Cabinet approve the
procurement approach for appointing an external Fund Manager for
the Business Northumberland Investment Fund and agree that on
conclusion of the procurement, and prior to award of contracts to
successful bidders, to receive an update for
consideration;
 
(i)       Cabinet agree that
the Business Northumberland Investment Fund be structured as a
Limited Partnership, with the Fund Manager acting as General
Partner and the Council as Limited Partner;
(j)       Cabinet confirm the
Governance arrangements for the Northumberland Growth Fund with
Cabinet having decision making authority, approving a programme
level approach and the NCC Programme Board having overall
responsibility for effective delivery of the relevant
programmes;
 
(k)      Cabinet agree to receive
regular updates on the implementation, performance and impact of
the Strategy and the Northumberland Growth Fund, including annual
reporting through the Council’s performance
framework;
 
(l)       Cabinet note that
NGF funding will be received by the Council in phases, subject to
the achievement of defined milestones linked to the Cambois Data
Centre Campus development;
 
(m)     Cabinet note that the scale,
phasing and deployment of the Northumberland Growth Fund, including
the commitment of any additional funds into the Economic
Infrastructure Programme or the Business Northumberland Investment
Fund, will be subject to further Cabinet approval; and
 
(n)      no steps will be taken to
progress resolutions (d) to (m) above until the report has been
considered by the Corporate Services and Economic Growth Overview
and Scrutiny Committee on 30 March 2026 and, if applicable, by
Cabinet on 7 April 2026 to consider Scrutiny’s
recommendations.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to endorse the Northumberland Economic Strategy 2035 and approve the approach for the Northumberland Growth Fund.

content:

that Cabinet approve as follows:-

Training Facility Remedial Works
 
a)

remedial works to be carried out at the Pegswood Breathing

Service, creating a new improved way of supporting in person
customer contact across a future blended Library and Information
Service.

that:-
 
(a)      Cabinet
note the methodology and activity undertaken to review the current
service operating models and inform the proposals for a new
integrated Library and Information Service;
 
(b)      Cabinet
note the proposals to create a new Library and Information Service
including the creation of a ‘universal front door’, the
introduction of an area based ‘hub and cluster’ model,
revised staff operating hours, extension of the network of
Community Access Libraries (CALs), making better use of digital
services, and redesign of the Mobile Library offer;
 
(c)      Cabinet
approve the commencement of an eight-week period of formal public
consultation, supported by a programme of awareness raising and
engagement, commencing Monday 16 February 2026 and concluding
Monday 13 April 2026; and
 
(d)      Cabinet
agree to receive a further report describing the findings from the
public consultation and final proposals for implementation of a new
Library and Information Service to be considered prior to
implementation.

RESOLVED
that:-
 

Queen’s Hall Theatre and Arts
Centre

Cabinet approve a grant of £0.150 million from
the Property Stewardship Fund (£0.050 million) and Strategic
Regeneration Fund (£0.100 million) to support Queen’s
Hall Arts with its capital investment programme to be scheduled in
2026-27.

Cabinet note that the £0.100 million grant
from the Strategic Regeneration Fund is potentially repayable by
Queen’s Hall Arts to the Council upon receipt of grant
funding from the Arts Council England.

Cabinet approve the amendment to the capital
programme to reallocate £0.050 million from the Property
Stewardship Fund and £0.100 million from the Strategic
Regeneration Fund to the Queen’s Hall Theatre and Arts Centre
project in 2026-27.

Lindisfarne Park, Alnwick

Cabinet approve capital spend totalling £0.092
million for the creation of a new public park at the old
Lindisfarne Middle School site in Alnwick in 2025-26, funded by the
Parks Enhancement Capital Programme and a £0.005 million
contribution from Councillor Gordon Castle’s MLIS
funds.

Cabinet approve the amendment to the capital
programme to reallocate £0.087 million in 2025-26 from the
Parks Enhancement Capital Programme project to the Lindisfarne Park
project.

Cramlington Regeneration Programme

Cabinet approve the spend of £1.500 million to
undertake the construction of the Northburn Sports and Community
Centre Masterplan Phase 1 (3G Football Pitch and Car Park) project
in financial year 2026-27. This is to be funded with £0.250
million from the remaining MTFP allocation for the Cramlington
Regeneration Programme, £0.100 million from the Sports
Development Reserve, £0.050 million contribution from
Cramlington United Football Club, and £1.100 million grant
from the Football Foundation.

Cabinet agree to accept Football Foundation funding
of £1.100 million and enter into a Grant Funding Agreement
with the Football Foundation for the above project, subject to
agreement of terms and receipt of appropriate legal advice.?Agree
to award a contract to a supplier to deliver the project subject to
procurement.

Cabinet approve the amendments to the capital
programme to reallocate £0.250 million from the Cramlington
Regeneration Programme to the Northburn Sports and Community Centre
Masterplan Phase 1 project and to add in the additional funding of
£1.250 million from the sources mentioned in 3.4a.

Cabinet approve a total funding allocation of
£0.350 million to deliver the Cramlington Alexandra Park
Skatepark redevelopment in 2026-27, including renovation and
expansion funded from the Cramlington Regeneration Programme
included in the MTFP.

Cabinet approve the amendment to the capital
programme to reallocate £0.350 million from the Cramlington
Regeneration project to the Cramlington Alexendra Skatepark in
2026-27.

Cabinet approve the sum of £0.205 million,
previously earmarked for the Dementia Garden project in
Cramlington, to be reallocated back to the Cramlington Regeneration
Programme budget for use on other projects following the Dementia
Garden project securing other funding and the contribution required
from the Council reducing to £0.050 million.

purpose:

consultation on School Admission Arrangements for Community and
Voluntary Controlled Schools and the Home to School Transport
Policy. Approval (determination) of the Admission Arrangements and
Home to School Transport Policy is also sought.
content:
RESOLVED
that:-
 
(a)      Cabinet
note the outcomes of the six-week consultation undertaken in
relation to the Council’s proposed admissions arrangements
for community and voluntary controlled schools for 2027/2028 and
the Council’s School Transport Policy for Children of
Compulsory School Age that took place between 3 November and 12
December 2025;
 
(b)      Cabinet
approve the proposed co-ordinated admissions scheme for all
maintained schools and academies, as provided in Appendix 1 of this
report;
 
(c)      Cabinet
approve (determine) the proposed final admissions arrangements for
2027/28, including proposed oversubscription criteria and proposed

as provided in Appendix 4 of this report.  These arrangements include the amendments to the

sixth forms, as provided in Appendix 5 of this report.  These arrangements include the amendments to the

letter of 5 January 2026;
 
(e)      Cabinet
approve the proposed reduction of the Planned Admission Number

2027;
 
(f)       in
the light of the determination letter received from the

Council’s Admissions Policy for primary and secondary
admissions into community and VC schools for 2026/27, provided at
Appendix 6 and 7 of this report; and
 
(g)      Cabinet
approve the Council’s School Transport Policy for Children of
Compulsory School Age 2025 provided in Appendix 8 of this
report.

content:

that:-

Housing Revenue Account 2026-27 budget as detailed within Appendix
1, which will reduce the balance on the HRA reserve from
£21.996 million at 31 March 2026,
to £14.021 million at 31 March
2027; and note the indicative budgets to 2029-30 which will reduce
the balance of the HRA reserve to £13.909 million;
 
(b)      Cabinet note that from 1
April 2026, social housing rent will be increased by Consumer Price
Index (CPI) plus 1.00% as per the previously agreed Rent Standard.
The budget detailed in Appendix 1 assumes that rents will rise by
CPI 3.80% plus 1.00% with recoverable service charges also rising
by CPI plus 1.00% for the period 1 April 2026 to 31 March
2027;
 
(c)      Cabinet approve the
increase of 4.80% for housing rents from 1 April 2026 in line with
the Government rent standard;
 
(d)      Cabinet approve the
increase of 4.80% for housing service charges from 1 April
2026;
 
(e )     Cabinet approve the
Non-Recurrent Growth Item of £1.000 million to deal with the
influx of queries and repairs relating to Damp and Mould following
the introduction of Awaab’s Law in October 2025 (detailed in
point 6.13);
 
(f)       Cabinet approve the
Non-Recurrent Growth Item of £0.135 million for 2026-27 and
2027-28 for additional Council tax on void properties (detailed in
point 6.13);
 
(g)      Cabinet approve the
Non-Recurrent Growth Item of £0.145 million for 2026-27 and
2027-28 for additional consumable materials for electrical testing
(detailed in point 6.13);
 
(h)      Cabinet approve the
Non-Recurrent Growth Item of £0.052 million for 2026-27 and
£0.053 million in 2027-28 for an Assistant Project Manager
post to coordinate the Energy Company Obligation/Great British
Insulation Scheme (ECO4/GBIS) delivery programme to lever in
external funding to supply energy efficient measures to the HRA
housing stock (detailed in point 6.13);
 
(i)       Cabinet approve the
Non-Recurrent Growth Item of £1.400 million for Stock
Condition Surveys to comply with The Regulator of Social Housing,
to be completed by 31 March 2027 (detailed in point
6.13);
 
(j)       Cabinet approve the
estimated pay inflationary increase for 2026-27 of 3.50%, pay
increments and National minimum wage increase totalling
£0.565 million (detailed in point 6.11);
 
(k)      Cabinet approve the
Non-Pay Inflation Schedule for 2026-27 totalling £0.283
million (detailed in point 6.11);
(l)       Cabinet approve the
Recurrent Growth Item of £0.093 million to fund additional
transport costs for the damp and mould and electrical testing teams
(detailed in point 6.12);
 
(m)     Cabinet approve the expenditure
plan relating to £26.539 million which has been set aside
over the 4-year period 2026-27 to 2029-30 in the HRA Capital
programme to invest in the Affordable Housing Investment Programme.
Details are set out in Appendix 1;
 
(n)      Cabinet approve the
expenditure plan relating to £52.461 million which has been
set aside over the 4-year period 2026-27 to 2029-30 in the HRA
Major Repairs Programme to invest in continued improvement to the
HRA housing stock. Details are set out in Appendix 1;
and
 
(o)      Cabinet note the
indicative 30-year Housing Revenue Account business plan as
detailed within Appendix 1.

purpose:
Statutory obligations have been placed on
English LA’s under the Environment Act 2021 to collect a more
consistent range of household waste materials for recycling, in
accordance with the Government’s National Resources and Waste
Strategy Consistency requirements.?

From 31st March 2026, the council will have a legal duty to ensure
dry recyclable materials and food waste are collected separately
from household residual waste. This will include a separate
collection of additional: Plastic pots, tubs and trays, glass
bottles and jars, tetra packs and flexible plastics;

Management of this increased range of materials will require a
major capital investment/rebuild of our existing MRF at West
Sleekburn. This paper provides cabinet with a detailed look at
several collection/processing option and requests a decision based
on this information for the way forward.
content:
RESOLVED
that:-
 
(a) Cabinet approves Option 3a (detailed in Section 7 of the report)
as the preferred option as it is the most efficient and effective
collection model for delivery of expanded household recycling
collections in Northumberland in full compliance with Simpler
Recycling requirements;
 
(b) Cabinet confirms that the
new recycling bin for paper, card and cardboard to be supplied to
each household under Option 3a will be a black bodied bin with a
burgundy coloured lid;
 
(c) Cabinet notes that the
earliest realistic but still challenging timeframe for
implementation of the new collection service under Option 3a would
be October 2026, but that there remain significant risks to
achievement of this timeframe and that the firm dates for
implementation can only be determined once all PFI Contract
negotiations have been concluded. The detail of proposed
implementation arrangements will therefore be the subject of
further reports to Cabinet in due course; and
 
(d) authority be delegated to
the Executive Director of Place and Regeneration in consultation
with the Cabinet Member for Environment, Rural and Farming to agree
the commercial terms and contract amendments to the Waste PFI
Contract and to provide the necessary contractual instruction to
Northumberland Energy Recovery Limited (NERL), the Councils PFI
partner to proceed with Option 3a.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve Option 3a for expanded household recycling collections in Northumberland.
